Verified in source. The cloud copy is started and not awaited (LandingStep.tsx:34) and the Dashboard link can be used at once (line 95, a plain link, so the page is replaced). The copy is one awaited request after another: the ICP, each account then its signal, then each deal (cloud-mirror.ts:75-140). Requests not yet started when the page is left never run. Both owning areas replace the device copy with the cloud as soon as the cloud holds one row: Signal Console ('Cloud has data → cloud is canonical. Replace local state.', signal-console/lib/cloud-persistence.ts:92-103) and Deal Workspace (loadDeals: setAllDeals then publishExternalState, which rewrites gtmos_deal_workspaces, deal-workspace/lib/persistence.ts:81-91, 22-25). So a user who clicks through within the first seconds can lose the accounts and deals that had not reached the cloud. Not run against a database, so medium confidence is right; the severity is right because it is silent loss of entered data on the main path. Holding the button until the copy settles (with a time limit), writing the deals first and sending the account inserts together is a contained change; the reader-side protection is correctly routed to the two owning areas.

The constants are real: the default flow writes qualityScore: 78, qualityBand: 'ready' (seed-writer.ts:71-72) and the two fallback flows write 60 / 'workable' (src/onboarding/lib/seed.ts:164-165); nothing computes them. Readiness reads the stored number (dashboard/lib/readiness-aggregator.ts:94) and awards the ICP-quality points for it (lib/readiness/dimensions.ts:48-55). Correction to where a user sees it: the default Dashboard's readiness review does not print evidence lines (dashboard/v4/ClimbDrawer.tsx:131-162 shows the next-state list and one word per area), so 'Best ICP quality: 78/100' appears on the previous Dashboard versions (dashboard/today/components/ReadinessPanel.tsx:92-94; dashboard/components/ReadinessDrawer.tsx:158-160) and in the readiness export and saved history; on the default screen the effect is the extra points, which lift the word shown for the ICP area. 'ready' is not read by anything (no reader of an ICP qualityBand exists in src). Removing both fields is safe: every reader treats a missing score as 0 (icp-studio/lib/persistence.ts:70; readiness-aggregator.ts:94; founding-gtm/lib/cross-room.ts:119), and Readiness then lists the true gap. Computing the score with ICP Studio's own engine is correctly left as an owner decision.

verdicts.reason: Verified. The map's step table, 'What it offers' table and guardrails say, as the current description of the first screen: 'Leads with the honesty — “this asks real work of you, here’s the deal.” The honest pitch, not an apology.', 'frames the friction as the sign they’re doing the rare thing', 'seeds Quota Workback + the outbound seed', 'Heavy-seeding doctrine #6' and 'Heavy-seeding — never re-soften…' (onboarding-capability-map-2026-07-07.html lines 40-41). The tester walkthrough's index page embeds this map (tools/preview/build-transcript.js:623; the generated index contains 'Leads with the honesty' and 'Heavy-seeding'), so it is read by testers as well as by writers. 'Honest', 'real work' / 'the work' and 'the rare thing' are the patterns COPY_STANDARD §26 removed from that screen; 'heavy-seeding' and 'seed' are the terms the original doctrine rewrite replaces (03_INTERNAL_LANGUAGE_DOCTRINE_REWRITE.md lines 19-20; 02_LANGUAGE_MIGRATION_MAP.md lines 51-53). The banner at the top of the map does not mark these rows as history. The replacement rows describe the shipped first screen and the quota step accurately and use the doctrine rewrite's own terms.

Each row was checked against source and none matches the shipped flow: (a) the ICP step is three multiple-choice questions with a typed alternative and accepts any answer (IcpStep.tsx:18-24; walk output line 59); (b) no company data is collected (industry, employees and headquarters are written empty, seed-writer.ts:107-112); (c) research covers the first 12 companies (index.ts:24, 120); (d) the deal form takes a typed account name, SeedDeal.enrichedSignal is never set (only declared, draft.ts:13), there is no budget or timeline field, and the flow enforces one deal and suggests ten (DealsStep.tsx:121, 146-163); (e) every note has source: null (evidence.ts:17-67); (f) nothing asks follow-up questions after setup; (g) the default flow does not record completion in the cloud and its button opens the Dashboard (LandingStep.tsx:22-35, 95). The map is embedded in the tester walkthrough, so these rows read as product capabilities. The replacement rows are accurate. Two adjustments: 'ten live deals' as the bar is a rule in the governing canon for this area (CLAUDE.md Part I §4.3: required ICP + account list + ≥10 live deals, fewer allowed with a plain note), so the map should state what the flow enforces without rewording that rule into 'one required' on its own authority; and row (g) must follow ONBOARDING-009 if that fix lands.
verdicts.finalProposed: Rows (a), (b), (c), (e), (f) as proposed. (d) 'The seller enters each open deal: account, value, stage, champion, who signs, and what is holding it up. Each added deal gets a card naming what to confirm next. Ten open deals is the target; the flow lets the seller continue with fewer (at least one) and says the workspace then has less to compare.' Tier row 'Required' → 'ICP + at least five target companies + open deals (ten is the target; at least one is enforced).' 'The ≥10-deal minimum' (capability row and guardrail) → 'The ten-deal target, with a plain note when fewer are entered'. (g) '… completion is recorded on the device; the ICP, accounts, signals and deals are copied to the cloud. Opens the Dashboard.' (change to 'recorded on the device and in the cloud' if ONBOARDING-009 is fixed). Any change to the ten-deal rule itself is a canon change for the owner (CLAUDE.md Part IV §4).

Every route that sends a new user to onboarding carries seeding=1: js/supabase-config.js:140 and :849, index.html:61, signup.html:171, auth/callback/index.html:69 (login.html:81 alone uses '/onboarding/', and only as a fallback).
